articles.title: Guided tours
articles.summary: Short tours that point at the real controls on a practice board. Nothing you do in a tour is saved.
articles.body:
A guided tour points at the real controls one at a time and waits while you try each one. There are three, a few minutes each:

- **Your first turn**: the mulligan, the board, inking and playing a card, reading a card, ending the turn, playing the other side, [Undo](help:undo) and where the [Multiverse](help:multiverse) is.
- **The Multiverse**: on a copy of the Set 13 demo. Open it, read and select a node, **Play from here**, branches, saving the turn you're in, the plot view, and the mini map (desktop) or the thumb keys (phone).
- **Study a Duels.ink game**: the paste field, the example log, the readout, **Study this game** and the imported turns in the Multiverse.

## Start a tour

:::desktop
Open Help (the **?** in the top bar, or {key:?}). The tours are at the top of the list; a ✓ marks the ones you've finished.
:::

:::phone
Open Help from the **⋯** menu, or **Help** on the home screen. The tours are at the top of the list; a ✓ marks the ones you've finished.
:::

New players also see **Start tour** under the headline on the home screen. **Not now** hides it for good.

## During a tour

- Each step names the control to use. Steps that wait for you have **Skip this step**; the others have **Next** and **Back**.
- **Learn more** opens the article for that step. Close Help and the tour carries on.

:::desktop
Leave any time with the **✕** on the tour card, or {key:Esc}.
:::

:::phone
Leave any time with the **✕** on the tour card.
:::

## Good to know

- A tour plays on a practice board, marked **Practice · not saved**. Nothing you do there goes in your library, and the match you had open is waiting, as it was, when the tour ends.
- Want to keep the practice board? **Save a copy** in its banner makes it a session of your own, and ends the tour.
- Reloading the page ends a tour. Start it again from Help.

articles.title: Sessions save themselves
articles.summary: Every match is a session, kept on this device as you play, and listed under Pick up again.
articles.body:
A session is one match with its whole Multiverse. The Dojo keeps every session on this device as you play, so you never lose a match by closing the tab.

## What makes a session

A new session starts when you:

- press **Start match** on the home screen,
- open a saved session file,
- study a Duels.ink log or replay,
- open a demo (it opens as your own copy).

It gets a name from the decks, like *Amber/Steel vs Ruby/Sapphire*. You can rename it: see [Save, save as copy, rename](help:save-and-rename).

## Saving happens by itself

Every change you make is saved to this device about a second later, and again when you switch tabs or close the page. You don't have to press **Save**. Leaving to the home screen keeps the match too.

## Pick up again

The home screen's **Pick up again** box lists your last session first (**Resume**), then your most recent ones, then the demos (**Explore**). The match on the board says **Back to it**. **All sessions** opens the [Library](help:library) with every session you have.

[Show me](show:recent)

## Good to know

- Sessions live in this browser on this device. Clearing the site's data or closing a private window deletes them, and another browser or device doesn't have them. Export a file to keep a backup, or [sign in](help:account) to keep them in an account. See [Where your things are kept](help:storage).
- **Auto-save every turn** (in the side rail, or the ☰ menu on a phone) is different: it saves a node in the [Multiverse](help:auto-save) at each turn.
- If the Dojo can't save to this device, it tells you once: "Couldn't save to this device. Export the session to keep it."

articles.title: Save, save as copy, rename
articles.summary: Name the session, save it now, or save a copy to try something without touching the original.
articles.body:
Give the match on the board a name, save it on the spot, or split off a copy to try a different idea.

## Rename the session

:::desktop
Click the session title at the top left of the top bar, type a new name and press {key:Enter}. {key:Esc} puts the old name back.

[Show me](show:session-title)
:::

:::phone
The top bar has no title on a phone. Tap **⋯** › **Leave to the dojo** (the match stays saved), open **Library**, then the session's **⋯** › **Rename**.
:::

You can rename any session the same way from the [Library](help:library): **⋯** › **Rename**.

## Save now

The Dojo already saves as you play (see [Sessions save themselves](help:sessions)). **Save** writes it straight away and tells you so. If you're signed in, it also saves the session to your account: see [What goes to your account](help:account-sync).

:::desktop
Press the floppy-disk button next to the title.

[Show me](show:save)
:::

:::phone
Tap **⋯** in the top bar, then **Save**.
:::

## Save as copy

Use it before trying a risky line: the copy carries on, and the original stays as it was.

:::desktop
Press the copy button next to **Save**.
:::

:::phone
Tap **⋯**, then **Save as copy**.
:::

Name the copy and press **Save copy**. The copy becomes the session on the board. The original keeps everything up to that moment.

## Good to know

- A new copy is only on this device. Signed in, press **Save** to put it in your account too.
- To copy a session without opening it, use **⋯** › **Duplicate** in the Library.
- Viewing someone's shared link, **Save** saves your own copy of it. See [Open a link someone sent you](help:open-a-shared-link).

articles.title: The Library: sessions, decks, links
articles.summary: Everything you keep, on shelves by where it lives: this device, your account, built in, public links.
articles.body:
The Library holds every session and deck you keep, sorted onto shelves by where each one lives.

## Open the Library

On the home screen, press **Library** at the top, or **All sessions** in **Pick up again**. The figures on the button count your sessions on this device and, signed in, in your account. {key:Esc} or **×** closes it.

[Show me](show:library-button)

From a match, leave to the home screen first (see [The screen at a glance](help:screen-at-a-glance)).

## Three tabs

- **Sessions**: every match you've kept. **Open** loads one (**Back to it** for the match on the board). Its **⋯** menu has **Rename**, **Share a link**, **Duplicate**, **Export file (.dojo.json.gz)** and **Delete…**. **Import file** adds a session file: see [Export and import session files](help:files).
- **Decks**: your decks and the **Built in** ones. **You** and **Opponent** seat a deck for the next match. **New deck**, **Import .txt** and **From a replay** add one. See [Your decks](help:decks).
- **Links**: the share links you made, under **Public links**. See [Share a deck or a session](help:share-links).

## The shelves

Signed out, your sessions and decks sit on **On this device**, with an empty **Your account** shelf that offers **Sign in**. Signed in, they sort into **In your account + this device**, **Only on this device** and **Only in your account**. Each shelf says in one line what that means.

A row only adds a note when it's out of step, like **Changed here since your last Save**. See [What goes to your account](help:account-sync).

:::phone
Each row's buttons sit at the foot of its card.
:::

## Good to know

- **Delete…** on a session or deck can't be undone. Export a session first if you might want it back.
- **On this device** means this browser only: clearing its site data deletes them. See [Where your things are kept](help:storage).

articles.title: Export and import session files
articles.summary: Save a session as a file to back it up or send it, and open a session file.
articles.body:
A session file holds a whole match: the board, every Multiverse node, the notes and the log. Export one to keep a backup outside this browser, or to send it to someone by hand.

## Export a session

- **The match on the board:** open the **Multiverse** and press **Export** at the top.
- **Any session:** in the Library, open the session's **⋯** and choose **Export file (.dojo.json.gz)**.

:::phone
In the Multiverse the file tools show only their icons: **Export** is the file with an arrow pointing out.
:::

[Show me](show:tree-export)

The file is named after the session, like `T8 study.dojo.json.gz` (characters a file name can't hold, such as `/`, are left out). It's compressed, so even a big Multiverse stays small. A browser that can't compress saves a plain `.dojo.json` instead.

## Open a session file

Any of these works:

- On the home screen, press **Choose a file**, or drop the file anywhere on the page. The Dojo reads it and shows **Saved session**. Press **Open it**.
- In the Library's **Sessions** tab, press **Import file**.
- In the Multiverse, press **Import**.

[Show me](show:intake-file)

The Dojo reads `.dojo.json.gz`, `.dojo.json` and older `.json` session files.

## Good to know

- Opening a file always adds a new session to your library and puts it on the board. Opening the same file twice gives you two sessions.
- Your files never go anywhere unless you send them. To send a match without a file, make a [share link](help:share-links).
- A file made by a newer Dojo asks you to reload the page to update first.

articles.title: Share a deck or a session
articles.summary: Make a short link to a deck or a whole multiverse; anyone can open it, no account needed.

headings.text: Share the match on the board

articles.body:
A share link sends a deck, or a whole match with its Multiverse, to anyone. They open it in their browser; neither of you needs an account.

## Share the match on the board

:::desktop
Press the share button next to **Save** in the top bar.

[Show me](show:share)
:::

:::phone
Tap **⋯** in the top bar, then **Share link**.
:::

## Share from the Library

- **A session:** in **Sessions**, open its **⋯** and choose **Share a link**.
- **A deck:** in **Decks**, open its **⋯** and choose **Share a link**. Built-in decks can be shared too.

## Copy the link

When it's ready, the **Link ready** box shows a short link like `practicedojo.win/app/?s=k3J9xQ2mPa`. Press **Copy link**, then paste it wherever you like.

## See and delete your links

The Library's **Links** tab lists your links under **Public links**. Press **Copy link** to copy one again. Its **⋯** has **Open in a new tab** and **Delete link**. A deleted link stops working for everyone: it opens as "This share is no longer available".

[Show me](show:lib-links)

## Good to know

- A link is a snapshot. Later changes aren't in it, so share again to send a newer version.
- Anyone who has the link can open it. A session link carries everything in the session, including your notes.
- Making a link needs a connection. The first time, the Dojo quietly gives this browser its own sharing identity; there's no sign-in screen.
- Signed out, the **Links** tab lists the links made from this browser, and clearing its site data loses that list (the links keep working). Signed in, links belong to your account, and links this browser made before you signed in come with you (unless that Discord or Google account was already a Dojo account).
- There are limits: 20 links a day, 100 in all, and sessions up to 10 MB compressed. See [Share link limits](help:share-limits).

articles.title: Open a link someone sent you
articles.summary: A shared session opens on the board unsaved until you save a copy; a shared deck lands on the home screen.
articles.body:
Open the link in your browser. You don't need an account, and nothing is saved until you choose to keep it.

## A shared session

The match opens on the board with a bar at the top: **Shared** · its title · **not saved yet** · **Save a copy**.

[Show me](show:shared-banner)

Look around, play on, open the Multiverse. While the bar shows, nothing goes into your library. To keep it, press **Save a copy** (**Save** in the top bar does the same). It becomes your own session on this device, under the same title, and saves itself from then on like any other.

If you open something else instead, or reload the page, your changes to the shared match are gone. A reload opens the link again from the start.

## A shared deck

The Dojo opens the home screen with the deck in the paste field, marked **Shared deck** with its name. Press **Play it as you** or **Play against it** to seat it, or **Save to My decks** to keep it.

[Show me](show:intake)

## If it doesn't open

- **Link not recognised:** part of the link is missing. Ask for it again, or check you copied all of it.
- **This share is no longer available:** the person who shared it deleted it.
- **Couldn't open the link:** the Dojo couldn't reach the sharing service. Check your connection and try again.

## Good to know

- Your copy is yours. Changing it never changes the link or the sharer's session.
- A shared link is a snapshot of the moment it was made. If they keep playing, ask for a new link.

articles.title: Why sign in (and why you don't have to)
articles.summary: Everything works signed out; signing in keeps your decks and sessions on every device.
articles.body:
An account is optional. It keeps your decks and sessions somewhere other than this browser, so they're on your other devices too: every device you sign in on.

## Signed out, everything works

You can play, use the Multiverse, study Duels.ink games, keep decks and sessions in the Library, export files, and make and open share links, all without an account. Signed out, nothing about accounts loads: the Dojo only goes online to load itself and the cards, and when you make or open a share link.

The catch: your library lives only in this browser on this device. Clearing the site's data, or closing a private window, deletes it, and another browser or device doesn't have it. Exporting files is the way to keep a backup. See [Where your things are kept](help:storage).

## What signing in adds

- **Decks follow you.** A deck you save goes to your account by itself and shows up on your other devices.
- **Sessions when you press Save.** **Save** puts the match in your account; play on another device and open it from the Library.
- **The Library shows where things are.** Its shelves sort everything by place: in your account, only on this device, or only in your account.
- **Your share links** belong to your account.

The details are in [What goes to your account](help:account-sync).

## Good to know

- You sign in with Discord or Google. See [Sign in and out](help:sign-in).
- An account holds up to 50 sessions and 200 decks. Sessions that don't fit can stay on this device.
- Your Tweaks (theme, card size and the rest) stay with this browser; they don't go to your account.
- Signing in needs a connection. If the account can't be reached, everything on this device still works.

articles.title: Sign in and out
articles.summary: Sign in with Discord or Google, choose what to bring from this device, and sign out safely on a shared computer.
articles.body:
Sign in to keep your decks and sessions in an account. It's optional; see [Why sign in](help:account).

## Sign in

1. On the home screen, press **Sign in** at the top. (The Library's **Your account** shelf has a **Sign in** button too.)
2. Choose **Continue with Discord** or **Continue with Google**.
3. Approve the Dojo on Discord's or Google's page. You come back to the Dojo, signed in, and the button shows your name.

[Show me](show:account-button)

The Dojo gets your name, picture and email from Discord or Google. It never sees your password.

## Bring what's on this device

The first time you sign in on a device that already has decks or sessions, the Dojo asks whether to save them to your account:

- **All** saves every one.
- **Choose…** opens the Library, where **Save to account** (in a row's **⋯**) or **Save all N to account** (on the **Only on this device** shelf) saves one row or a whole shelf.
- **Not now** leaves them on this device only. You can still save them from the Library later.

Either way, they stay on this device too.

## Your account

Press your name on the home screen to see who you're signed in as and how much of your account you use (up to 50 sessions and 200 decks).

## Sign out

Press your name, then **Sign out**. The Dojo asks about the copies of your account's decks and sessions on this device:

- **Keep on this device**: they stay here, for you or anyone using this browser.
- **Remove from this device**: use this on a shared computer. Your account keeps everything either way.

Sessions and decks that were never in an account stay on the device either way.

## Good to know

- Share links you made from this browser before signing in move to your account. If your Discord or Google account was already a Dojo account, the Dojo offers to sign in to it instead, and those links stay with this browser.

articles.title: What goes to your account, and conflicts
articles.summary: Decks follow you automatically; sessions go up when you press Save; what happens when two devices disagree.

headings.text: Sessions go up when you press Save

articles.body:
Signed in, decks reach your account by themselves, and sessions reach it when you press **Save**. Nothing merges in the background, so you always know which copy is where.

## Decks follow you

Saving a deck on this device also saves it to your account. Your other devices pick it up when you sign in or open the Library's **Decks** tab. If two devices edit the same deck, the last save wins. Deleting a deck that's in your account deletes it from both.

## Sessions go up when you press Save

While you play, the session saves to this device only. **Save** in the top bar (on a phone, **⋯** › **Save**) also saves it to your account. A session that's already in your account is saved there again when you switch tabs or close the page with unsaved changes.

[Show me](show:save)

## Read the Library

In **Sessions**, a row says when its two copies differ:

- **Changed here since your last Save**: press **Save to account**.
- **Your account has a newer copy**: press **Get newer copy** to replace this device's copy with it.
- On the **Only in your account** shelf, **Download & open** brings a session to this device.

## When two devices disagree

If the session changed in your account since this device last saved it, **Save** asks **This session changed on another device**:

- **Overwrite with mine**: your account keeps this device's version.
- **Save mine as a copy**: this version goes to your account as a new session, and the other stays.
- **Cancel**: nothing is saved to your account.

## Good to know

- Deleting a session that's in both places asks **This device**, **Account** or **Both**.
- If saving to your account fails, the match is still saved on this device.
- An account holds up to 50 sessions and 200 decks, and a session up to 10 MB compressed.

articles.title: Tweaks
articles.summary: Where the settings are and what each one changes.
articles.body:
Tweaks is where the Dojo's settings live: how it looks, how big the cards are, and how much it tells you about a challenge.

## Open Tweaks

:::desktop
Press the sliders button at the right end of the top bar. Press it again, or **×**, to close.

[Show me](show:tweaks)
:::

:::phone
Tap **⋯** in the top bar, then **Tweaks**. Tap **×** to close.
:::

Tweaks opens from a match. On the home screen, only the theme can be changed (the **Auto / Day / Night** switch at the top).

## What's in it

- **Theme**: **Auto**, **Day** or **Night**. See [Day, night and accent](help:theme).
- **Accent**: the colour of the main buttons and highlights. See [Day, night and accent](help:theme).
- **Card size**: how big cards are. See [Card size and Art / Text](help:card-display).
- **Card display**: **Art** or **Text** for every card. See [Card size and Art / Text](help:card-display).
- **Challenge forecast**: **Off**, **Light** or **Full**. See [Challenge forecast](help:forecast).
- **Player palette**: **Competition**, **Modern** or **Mono**. See [Player palette](help:palette).

## Good to know

- A change shows straight away; there's nothing to save.
- Tweaks are kept in this browser. They don't go to your account, and clearing the site's data resets them.

articles.title: Day, night and accent
articles.summary: Follow your device's light or dark setting, or pick Day or Night, and choose the accent colour.
articles.body:
The **Theme** setting picks a light or dark Dojo; **Accent** picks the colour that marks the main button and where you are.

## Choose the theme

In [Tweaks](help:tweaks), **Theme** has three choices:

- **Auto** follows your device's light or dark setting, and changes when it does.
- **Day** is always the warm light look.
- **Night** is always the warm dark look.

[Show me](show:tweak-theme)

On the home screen, the **Auto / Day / Night** switch at the top is the same setting.

[Show me](show:home-theme)

## Choose the accent

**Accent** has four swatches. Its current name shows beside the label.

- **Signal** is the theme's own: orange by day, a brighter orange at night.
- **Coral**, **Olive** and **Trace** use that colour in both themes.

The accent colours the main button in each view, like **End turn** and **Start match**, and the marks that show where you are, like the turn number and the line you're on in the Multiverse.

[Show me](show:tweak-accent)

## Good to know

- Your choices are kept in this browser. The Practice Dojo website follows the same theme.
- The players' colours are a separate setting: [Player palette](help:palette).

articles.title: Card size and Art / Text
articles.summary: Make cards bigger or smaller, and show card art or text-only cards everywhere.
articles.body:
Two settings in [Tweaks](help:tweaks) change how cards look: **Card size** and **Card display**.

## Card size

Drag the **Card size** slider. It goes from 0.70× to 1.40×, and the value shows beside the label. It starts at 1.00×, or 0.80× on a touch screen so the board fits a phone.

[Show me](show:tweak-card-size)

When the play area fills up, cards in play still shrink to fit, whatever the setting.

## Art or Text

**Card display** has two choices:

- **Art** shows the card pictures. A card whose picture can't be fetched shows as text instead.
- **Text** shows every card as text: name, version, cost, stats and rules. No card pictures are loaded at all.

[Show me](show:tweak-card-display)

It applies everywhere at once: the board, your hand, the inkwell, the discard, every card grid and the card preview. On a text card, a gold disc means inkable and a dark hexagon means not inkable.

## Good to know

- **Text** is handy on a slow or no connection, since it needs no pictures. See [Playing offline](help:offline).
- Both settings are kept in this browser.

articles.title: Player palette
articles.summary: How the two players are coloured: by their deck's inks, two fixed colours, or grey.
articles.body:
**Player palette** in [Tweaks](help:tweaks) sets how the Dojo tells the two players apart by colour.

## Choose a palette

[Show me](show:tweak-palette)

- **Competition** (the default): each side is shaded in its own deck's two inks, on the board, the player rows, the lore and the Multiverse nodes. Player 1's mark is split in two; Player 2's is striped like a barber pole, so a mirror match still reads. Under the switch, a P1 and a P2 icon show the inks it picked; hover one to see their names. Before both decks are known, it uses Modern's colours.
- **Modern**: two fixed colours, olive for Player 1 and teal for Player 2, whatever the decks.
- **Mono**: grey only. There's no colour anywhere, card pictures included. Player 1 is light and Player 2 is heavy.

## Good to know

- The palette only changes the players' colours. The light or dark look is the [Theme](help:theme).
- It's kept in this browser.

articles.title: Challenge forecast
articles.summary: How much the Dojo shows about a challenge before you make it: off, one line, or the full forecast.
articles.body:
**Challenge forecast** sets how much the Dojo tells you about a [challenge](help:challenge) before you make it: who would be banished and how much damage each card would have.

## Choose how much

In [Tweaks](help:tweaks), **Challenge forecast** has three choices: **Off**, **Light** (the default) and **Full**.

[Show me](show:tweak-forecast)

:::mouse
While you drag your character onto an opponent's card, or point at one in challenge mode:

- **Off** shows only the arrow.
- **Light** shows one line over the target: who gets banished, and the damage after.
- **Full** shows a forecast card with each card's damage before and after, marked **BANISHED** or **SURVIVES**, and the extra damage on both cards. Once you pick an attacker in challenge mode, every opponent card also gets an outcome badge.

The challenge mode bar has the same **Off / Light / Full** switch, so you can change it mid-challenge.

[Show me](show:challenge-banner)
:::

:::touch
With no pointer to hover, **Light** and **Full** both work the same way: once you pick your character in challenge mode, every opponent card gets an outcome badge. **Off** shows no badges.
:::

## Good to know

- The forecast only predicts. The Dojo never stops a challenge: if your character is exerted or drying, it lets you and says so.
- The setting is kept in this browser.

home-button.label: the way back to the home screen (‹ Dojo)

text.desktop: This is a practice board with two Set 13 decks. Nothing you do here is saved. Leave any time with **✕** or Esc.
text.phone: This is a practice board with two Set 13 decks. Nothing you do here is saved. Leave any time with **✕**.

text.desktop: First, your opening hand. Click cards to send them to the bottom and press **Mulligan**, or press **Keep hand**.
text.phone: First, your opening hand. It's a good one: tap **Keep hand**. (Another time, tap cards first to send them to the bottom.)

steps.text: The bottom half is the player whose turn it is: the hand, the play area and the inkwell. The other player's side is at the top.

text.desktop: Put a card in your inkwell: drag it from your hand onto the inkwell, or hover it and press **INK**.
text.phone: Put a card in your inkwell: tap a card in your hand, then **Ink**.

hint.phone: Only inkable cards can be inked; the others say **No ink**.

text.desktop: Now play a card: drag a 1-cost character onto your play area, or hover it and press **PLAY**.
text.phone: Now play a card: tap a 1-cost character, then **Play**.

steps.hint: The cost is the number in the card's top-left corner.

steps.text: Hover any card on the board to read it here, full size: cost, strength, willpower, lore and text.
Tap a card in your hand to open its drawer: the card full size, and what you can do with it. Close it when you've read it.

text.desktop: Done for this turn? Press **End turn**, or the Space bar.
text.phone: Done for this turn? Tap **End turn**.

steps.text: Now you're Player 2: the board turns round, so their side is at the bottom. Settle their opening hand, then ink one of their cards.

text.desktop: Changed your mind? **Undo** takes back the last thing you did. Press it now to take that ink back.
text.phone: Changed your mind? **Undo** takes back the last thing you did. Tap it now to take that ink back.

steps.text: Every turn you end is kept as a node in the **Multiverse**. The mini map shows them here; **Multiverse** (or M) opens the whole tree.
Every turn you end is kept as a node in the **Multiverse**. This button opens the whole tree.
A practice copy of the Set 13 demo: a whole game, with the other ways it could have gone. Nothing you do here is saved.

text.desktop: Open the **Multiverse**: press it, or M.

steps.text: Every node is a saved turn: whose it was, the lore, what they played. Turns run left to right; where a line forks, the game went another way.

text.desktop: Click a node to select it. The arrow keys step through the tree too.
text.phone: Tap a node to select it.

steps.text: The panel shows the selected node. **Play from here** puts that board back on the table.

hint.desktop: Double-clicking a node, or Enter, does the same.

steps.text: Now play it differently: a new card, another challenge. When you end the turn, the Multiverse keeps both lines. That fork is a branch.

text.desktop: To keep a turn before it's over, press T (or **Save current unfinished turn** in the Multiverse), then **Save node**.
text.phone: To keep a turn before it's over, open the **Multiverse**, tap **Save current unfinished turn**, then **Save node**.

text.desktop: **Plot** shows every saved turn as a dot, so a long game fits on one screen. Press it.
text.phone: **Plot** switches between dots and cards. Tap it.

steps.text: The thumb keys step through the tree: ◀ ▶ the turn before and after, ▲ ▼ the line above and below, the circle back to where you are.
Close the Multiverse with **✕** to go back to the board.
On the board, the mini map keeps the tree in view: click a dot to go there, or step with its keys.
Paste a Duels.ink log or replay into this field, or drop the file on the page. The Dojo works out what it is.

text.desktop: No game to hand? Press **A Duels.ink log** for an example.
text.phone: No game to hand? Tap **A Duels.ink log** for an example.

steps.text: The readout says what it found: a Duels.ink log and how many turns it has.

text.desktop: Press **Study this game**. In the tour it opens as a practice board, so nothing goes in your library.
text.phone: Tap **Study this game**. In the tour it opens as a practice board, so nothing goes in your library.

steps.text: Every turn of the game is now a node. Open the **Multiverse** to see them.
Here's the game turn by turn. Select a node and **Play from here** to replay it. Cards the log never names stay unknown until you fill them in.
